forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Held at 22%. No lab or government has issued a formal AGI declaration and no convergence of 3+ leading researchers on 'achieved'. Davos 2026 positions persist: Amodei's 'nation of geniuses by 2027', Shane Legg ~50% Minimal AGI by 2028, Hassabis ~50% by 2030 with scientific/creative reasoning still lagging. Resolution bar unmet; nothing since last run moves the estimate.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: near-term insider predictions of a transformative technology arriving within a fixed ~3.5-year window, where insiders carry optimism incentives. Such forecasts resolve YES well under half the time; base ~15-20%.

factors_up.factor: Lab leadership timelines (Anthropic 'powerful AI' 2026-27; Legg ~2028) sit inside the window
Rapid frontier-model cadence and agentic progress in verifiable domains (coding, maths)

factors_down.factor: Resolution bar (credible declaration or 3+ researchers) remains unmet and definitionally contested
Hassabis and cautious voices keep the field short of a shared 'achieved' call; scientific discovery/creative reasoning still weak

key_uncertainties: Whether any major lab will formally declare 'AGI' rather than avoiding the term
Whether 3+ leading researchers would publicly converge on 'AGI achieved' before 2030
update_triggers: Revise UP if a credible lab announces AGI or 3+ leading researchers state it is achieved
Revise DOWN if labs explicitly push timelines beyond 2030

forecasts.question: Will economic consultancy lose ≥33% value/jobs by end 2030 due to AI?
forecasts.key_change: Nudged up from 26% to 27%. Fresh 2026 evidence of AI-linked contraction: McKinsey planning ~10% cuts (3,000-4,000 roles), Accenture cutting ~11,000 roles tied to changing work, Bain/BCG/Deloitte slowing hiring, graduate consulting postings down ~44% YoY. Trajectory is toward the threshold but current declines (~10%) are still far short of the 33% bar attributable primarily to AI by 2+ credible analyses.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: mature professional-services sectors experiencing a technology shock; historically employment/revenue contractions of >=33% within ~6 years attributable to a single cause are uncommon (base ~15-20%).

factors_up.factor: Concrete 2026 layoffs (McKinsey ~10%, Accenture ~11k) with AI cited as a driver
Structural pressure from AI-native boutiques and collapsing junior/analyst hiring

factors_down.factor: 33% decline from a 2024 baseline by 2030 is a high bar; current cuts ~10%
Attribution 'primarily to AI' is contested (also post-pandemic demand slowdown, cyclical factors)

key_uncertainties: Whether cuts accelerate from ~10% toward 33% by 2030 or plateau
Whether credible analyses will attribute declines primarily to AI vs. cyclical demand
update_triggers: Revise UP if cumulative headcount/revenue declines pass ~20% with explicit AI attribution
Revise DOWN if consulting demand rebounds or firms re-hire as AI augments rather than replaces

forecasts.question: Will Labour be largest party at next UK General Election?
forecasts.key_change: Held at 6%. Early-July 2026 polling still poor for Labour: averages put them ~18-22%, behind Reform UK (~26%) and near the Conservatives (~19%). Reform's sustained lead and continued fragmentation keep Labour's path to most seats narrow, though the next GE is not due until 2029, leaving room for recovery under FPTP.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: governing parties polling third/second ~3 years before an election going on to win most seats; uncommon but not negligible given FPTP and mid-term unpopularity that often partly reverses (base ~10-15%).

factors_up.factor: ~3 years to the election allows substantial recovery; incumbency and FPTP can convert modest vote share into seat pluralities
Multi-party fragmentation can hand pluralities on low vote shares

factors_down.factor: Reform UK holds a sustained polling lead; Labour support down sharply since 2024
Government approval near record lows with no clear recovery catalyst

key_uncertainties: Whether Reform's lead proves durable or reverts as an election nears
How fragmentation and tactical voting translate votes into seats under FPTP
update_triggers: Revise UP if Labour regains a consistent polling lead or Reform collapses
Revise DOWN if Reform's lead widens further or an early election is called

forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2035?
forecasts.key_change: Held at 83%. The longer ~9-year window comfortably contains most insider and community timelines (Amodei, Legg ~2028, Hassabis ~50% by 2030). Barring a fundamental scaling/algorithmic wall, a credible declaration or 3+ researcher convergence is likely within the decade. No change since last run.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: transformative-technology arrival within a ~9-year window where multiple credible insiders forecast success inside the horizon; such medium-horizon forecasts resolve YES more often than near-term ones (base ~55-65%).

factors_up.factor: Most leading-lab and community medians for AGI fall before 2035
Sustained compute scaling, capital inflows and rapid agentic progress

factors_down.factor: Definitional contestation could delay any clean 'achieved' declaration even if capabilities are high
Possible scaling/algorithmic or energy bottlenecks, or regulatory slowdowns

key_uncertainties: Whether capability gains continue or hit a wall this decade
Whether the community converges on a declaration even if AGI-like systems exist
update_triggers: Revise UP if a credible AGI declaration occurs or timelines compress
Revise DOWN if frontier progress visibly plateaus or a hard bottleneck emerges

forecasts.question: Will China initiate a military blockade or invasion of Taiwan before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Held at 7%. US intelligence assessments continue to judge an imminent PRC attack unlikely; Beijing prefers 'unification without force' and recognises an amphibious assault would be extremely costly. The PLA keeps building blockade/amphibious capability and grey-zone coercion around Taiwan and in the near seas, but a direct >72hr blockade or assault remains the low-probability tail through 2030.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: great-power initiations of a major blockade/invasion against a defended territory within a fixed ~4-year window; historically rare (base ~5%).

factors_up.factor: Growing PLA amphibious/blockade capability (third carrier, landing barges, port-blockade drills)
Sustained grey-zone coercion and paramilitary presence that could escalate by accident

factors_down.factor: US and analysts assess near-term direct action unlikely; Beijing prefers coercion short of war
High risk of failure and US intervention deters an amphibious assault

key_uncertainties: Whether grey-zone actions escalate into a formal >72hr blockade
Xi's internal timeline and risk tolerance
update_triggers: Revise UP on mobilisation, a declared quarantine/blockade, or a major cross-strait incident
Revise DOWN on cross-strait de-escalation or renewed dialogue

forecasts.question: Will UK annual CPI inflation fall below 2.0% for at least one month before 1 January 2027?
forecasts.key_change: Held at 2% (CI tightened to 1-4%). Latest ONS data shows CPI at 2.8% in May 2026, unchanged from April, with food inflation easing to 2.2%. Only ~6 monthly prints remain before Jan 2027, and a fall from a sticky 2.8% to below 2.0% within that window is unlikely on current trajectory. Window narrowing keeps this a low-probability outcome.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: sub-2.0% monthly CPI print occurring within a ~6-month window while inflation sits ~0.8pp above target and is described as sticky; uncommon absent a demand shock (base ~5%).

factors_up.factor: Food inflation easing (2.2% in May) and some disinflationary momentum
Possible energy/base effects or a demand shock could produce a single soft print

factors_down.factor: CPI stuck at 2.8% for two consecutive months, ~0.8pp above the 2% target
Few monthly prints remain before the Jan 2027 deadline

key_uncertainties: Whether services inflation and wage growth ease fast enough
Whether any one-off base effect drags a single month below 2.0%
update_triggers: Revise UP if a print lands at or near 2.0% or energy prices fall sharply
Revise DOWN if CPI reaccelerates or holds at/above 2.8%

forecasts.question: Will Spider-Man: Brand New Day gross over $1.5B worldwide by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Held at 93%. Tracking remains very strong ahead of the 31 July release: worldwide opening-weekend projections ~$550M, domestic ~$210-255M, best US presales in years. A ~$550M open with a typical 2.7-3.2x tentpole multiplier clears $1.5B comfortably (No Way Home did $1.9B). Minor headwinds: no domestic IMAX opening weekend (The Odyssey) and no China IMAX for two weeks slightly cap the ceiling.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: MCU/Spider-Man tentpoles with record presales and >$500M projected global openings; most such films clear $1.5B lifetime (base ~80-90%).

factors_up.factor: Record presales and ~$550M projected worldwide opening weekend
Franchise legs (No Way Home $1.9B) and full second half of 2026 to accumulate gross

factors_down.factor: No domestic IMAX opening weekend and no China IMAX for two weeks trims premium-format revenue
Execution/reception risk or a weaker-than-expected multiplier

update_triggers: Revise UP if opening weekend meets or beats ~$550M worldwide
Revise DOWN if reviews/word-of-mouth are poor or the opening underperforms tracking

forecasts.question: Will OpenAI and Anthropic have a combined ARR exceeding $70B by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Held at 99%. Current reporting already puts the combined figure near or above $70B: Anthropic ~$47B annualized (Sacra, May 2026) after hitting a $30B run rate in April, and OpenAI ~$33B run rate (May 2026). With both growing rapidly, the Q4 2026 sum comfortably exceeds $70B barring a catastrophic reversal.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: hyper-growth AI leaders already at/near a revenue threshold six months before the measurement date, growing multiple-x per year; near-certain to clear it (base >95%).

factors_up.factor: Combined annualized revenue already ~$80B by mid-2026 (Anthropic ~$47B + OpenAI ~$33B)

factors_down.factor: Definitional/reporting differences (ARR vs run-rate) and source disagreement
Tail risk of a severe demand or funding shock before Q4 2026

key_uncertainties: Which reported figure/definition resolvers use for Q4 2026 ARR
Whether any reversal or restatement occurs before year-end
update_triggers: Revise DOWN only on a major revenue collapse or restatement
Already near ceiling; little room to revise UP

forecasts.question: Will UK average annual real GDP growth exceed 1.5% across the 2030s (2030-2039)?
forecasts.key_change: Held at 38%. No new structural information this run. Mainstream long-run UK trend-growth estimates cluster around ~1.5%, placing the 10-year-average-above-1.5% threshold near a coin-flip but slightly below even. Upside from potential AI-driven productivity gains is offset by demographic headwinds and weak recent productivity trends.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: advanced-economy decade-average real GDP growth exceeding trend estimates; UK has undershot 1.5% average in recent decades post-2008 (base ~35-40%).

factors_up.factor: Potential AI/automation productivity boost across the decade
Possible investment/planning reforms lifting trend growth

factors_down.factor: Weak post-2008 productivity trend and ageing demographics
Fiscal constraints and recurring shock risk over a 10-year horizon

key_uncertainties: Whether AI materially lifts measured UK productivity this decade
Frequency/severity of shocks and the demographic/labour-supply path
update_triggers: Revise UP if productivity growth durably accelerates or OBR upgrades trend growth
Revise DOWN on a major recession or further productivity disappointment
